correctness.rationale: PASS: With r+1 colours on r nonempty pairwise-complete parts, any proper final colouring either has r monochromatic parts or one uniquely bichromatic fully seeded part. The missing-colour rule cannot start from any incomplete monochromatic pattern. In a split pattern, every vertex of the split part must be seeded, and at most one monochromatic part may have zero seeds; the converse follows by the unique forced first action. Counting (r+1)!/2 allocations, (2^{n_j}-2) surjective split assignments, and seeded-subset factors A_i proves the entire polynomial and its probability substitution. Minimum seed n_j+r-2 and multiplicity follow directly. Independent definitional brute force for K_{2,2,2}, four colours, gave coefficients 288,432,288,96 for domains 3..6; this is finite corroboration only.
